text: dsh-fracture（DSH 插件，通用客户端）：观察已完成的 DSH 会话，找出工具失败、重复读取、审批拒绝等 harness 问题，并把发现整理为改进建议。插件提供诊断、把任务转成验收条件、生成 harness 候选、对照运行当前与候选配置、整理通过探测的改动为可安装 bundle，以及跨会话记忆和技能蒸馏。候选先以数据形式保存并经探测比较；prompt 改动可按设置自动应用并观察，代码 bundle 仍由用户安装。需要 DSH 的 agent、会话和工具服务；Node.js 22 或更高版本。

dsh-fracture diagnoses DSH sessions, proposes harness improvements, and compares candidates with the current setup on the same task. It also keeps cross-session memory and distills repeated procedures into skills. Requires DSH agent services and Node.js 22 or later.

How can I diagnose recurring failures in my DSH sessions and improve the harness?
I want to compare a proposed harness change against the current setup before keeping it.
dsh-fracture 的功能「会话诊断」：读取近期已存会话并统计工具失败、重复读取、审批拒绝、压缩压力和反馈，输出带 finding 标识的诊断快照，供后续建议引用。
dsh-fracture 的功能「候选对照探测」：为同一任务分别运行当前 harness 和候选改动，比较结果并保存报告；没有确定性检查时会呈现待人工审阅的结果。
dsh-fracture 的功能「跨会话记忆与技能蒸馏」：在每个完整会话轮次后提取观察，定期更新记忆摘要，并将重复且无工具错误的步骤整理为技能供 agent 使用。

MEMORY.md] Two properties matter before reading the code:

dsh-fracture README · Architecture：- A candidate that ships a `plugin/` directory runs in a separate `dsh` process, so unverified code never loads in the process that judges it.
- Candidates that touch approval, sandbox policy, the plugin manager, or this plugin are rejected before they are stored, and again before they are probed.

The reasoning behind the tier boundaries is in [docs/仕組み.md](docs/仕組み.md) (Japanese).

dsh-fracture README · What it is：DSH builds an agent out of an ordered list of plugin rows. A model, a prompt section, a skill root, a tool, an approval policy: each is a row with its own config.

Two consequences follow. A harness is data, so a candidate harness is a diff against the current one. And two harnesses can exist at the same time, so a change can be judged by running the same task on both instead of asking a model whether its own idea sounds good.

dsh-fracture README · The problem：Three failures are common in a setup that nobody has time to tune.

**The same mistake outlives the session.** A tool fails because the project uses pnpm, or because the fixture has to be built before the test runs. The model works it out, the session ends, and the next session starts from nothing.

dsh-fracture README · The problem：**Harness tuning is guesswork.** Someone edits the system prompt, decides the agent feels better, and has no way to check. The edit stays. The next edit lands on top of it. Two months later nobody knows which line matters.

**Nothing accumulates.** When a session goes well, the procedure that made it go well is not written down anywhere the next session can read.

dsh-fracture README · The problem：All three have the same cause: nothing in the loop records what happened, and nothing tests a change against a baseline. Fracture adds both, and lets them run unattended.

dsh-fracture README · What it does：It records every finished turn as facts rather than prose: which tools ran, in which order, what failed, whether you had to step in and correct it. After twenty turns that log becomes a digest. After three clean repetitions of one procedure, the procedure becomes a skill. The digest and the skill list go into the prompt as a short index, so the agent knows what it has learned without loading everything it has recorded.
dsh-fracture README · What it does：It also changes the harness, but only where a measurement supports the change, and the depth of what it may change on its own is bounded:

dsh-fracture README · What it does：| Tier | What changes | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Memory | observations, digest, journal | none, additive |
| Skills | `skills/<slug>/SKILL.md`, registered live | none, additive |
| Composition | prompt rows, skill-dir rows, tool toggles | probe verdict plus a watch window, auto-revert on regression |
| Code | a candidate plugin module | **human**: `dsh plugin add` |

dsh-fracture README · What it does：The first two tiers are knowledge. They cannot execute anything, cannot widen a permission, and are removed by deleting a file, so they run without asking. The third is a data change the loop owns and can undo, so it runs without asking but is watched for twelve turns afterwards and reverted if the numbers get worse. The fourth decides what code runs inside your process, so the loop may author it and probe it, and you decide whether it runs.

dsh-fracture README · What it does：That last line is deliberate. An agent that can install its own code needs no human in the loop to do it, and its first bad change would then be the one change it cannot detect from the inside.

Everything it writes is a file you can read: `.dsh/fracture/`.

A distilled skill, an applied change, and a revert each post one collapsed notice into the session, so the loop never acts silently. Nothing else does, because a notice per turn stops being information.

dsh-fracture README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:miketako3/dsh-fracture
```

That is the distribution path. It installs from the repository and builds the package on the way in.

dsh-fracture README · Install：pnpm refuses to run build scripts of a git-hosted package by default, so the first attempt fails with `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED`. Copy the `allowBuilds` line the error prints into `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/pnpm-workspace.yaml` and run the command again. The key contains the fetched commit hash, so it changes whenever main moves.

Restart once. No configuration is required: observation and memory start immediately.

```yaml

dsh-fracture README · $DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml：- id: fracture
  name: dsh-fracture
  config:
    autonomy: full        # off | memory | skills | full
    baseDir: .dsh/fracture
    digestEvery: 20       # observed turns between digest rewrites
    distillMinRepeats: 3  # clean repetitions before a skill is written
    autoLoop: true        # let the 15 minute idle trigger run the whole loop
    autoApply: true       # apply a prompt-only candidate that probed improved
    watchTurns: 12        # turns watched before an applied change is kept
    maxWatches: 3         # changes watched at the same time
    judge: off            # off | rubric; score a candidate that has no check
```

dsh-fracture README · Tools：| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `fracture_diagnose` | Ranks what the current harness does badly: tool failure rates, repeated reads, denied approvals, compaction pressure, message feedback. |
| `fracture_propose` | Sends a proposer subagent to write one candidate as `candidate.json` plus optional `skills/` or `plugin/`. |
| `fracture_probe` | Runs a task on the current harness and on the candidate, then compares. Writes `runs/<id>/report.md`. |
| `fracture_plan` | Turn a request into checks that can be run or read |
| `fracture_adopt` | Turns a probed candidate into an installable bundle and appends the lesson. Never installs. |
| `fracture_status` | What was learned, what was proposed, how each candidate scored. |
| `fracture_loop` | Runs diagnose → propose → probe → apply once, with the same gates the idle trigger uses. |
| `memory_search` | Searches the digest, past turns, and distilled skills. |

dsh-fracture README · Documentation：The design and contribution documents are written in Japanese. That is a deliberate choice: they are read by the person who maintains the loop, and a translated design document loses the precision that makes it useful.

dsh-fracture README · Where the ideas come from：[Harness²](https://github.com/google-research/harness2) (Google Research, Apache-2.0) is the direct source for three ideas, all of which this plugin implements:

dsh-fracture README · Where the ideas come from：- **Contrast beats introspection.** Judge an edit by running the task on both harnesses, not by asking a model to review it.
- **Lessons accumulate with evidence.** Every adoption appends the cue, the change, the verdict, and a rationale to `lessons.md`.
- **Escalate from the weakest lever.** Prompt before skill, skill before script, script before tool, tool before hook.

dsh-fracture README · Where the ideas come from：Harness²'s eight-file harness tree is deliberately not adopted. DSH's row list already is that tree, with a loader and a diff, so copying the tree would add a second way to describe the same thing.

The rest is DSH's own material: plugin rows for composition, the `SKILL.md` convention for procedures, `session/event` for observation, and scoped prompt sections for injection. No Harness² code is vendored.

dsh-fracture README · Development：```bash
npm install && npm test     # 128 tests, node:test only
npm run build
npm run demo                # one loop over synthetic turns
```

Contributions are welcome, but read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first, because most changes here move a boundary rather than add a feature.

dsh-fracture README · Status：0.2 covers observation, memory, skill distillation, the live prompt section, the unattended loop, in-session notices, and automatic apply with auto-revert for prompt-level candidates. Row-shaped candidates still go through a bundle and a human.
